title: Equatorial sign records for adaptively corrupted DCP

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the equatorial sign transcript algorithm in proof.md recovers the entire shift with unconditional probability greater than 0.98 under either delivery process specified below. On every execution branch, total charged work is O(2^(n/2) n^3 log2 n), with an absolute constant and envelope growth index exactly 1. This guarantee holds jointly with the other resource and tolerance claims.

For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the equatorial sign transcript algorithm in proof.md recovers the entire shift with unconditional probability greater than 0.98 under either delivery process specified below. On every execution branch, peak allocated classical bits is O(n^2), with an absolute constant and envelope growth index exactly 0. This guarantee holds jointly with the other resource and tolerance claims.

For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the equatorial sign transcript algorithm in proof.md recovers the entire shift with unconditional probability greater than 0.98 under either delivery process specified below. On every execution branch, peak allocated qubits is O(n), with an absolute constant and envelope growth index exactly 0. This guarantee holds jointly with the other resource and tolerance claims.

For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the equatorial sign transcript algorithm in proof.md recovers the entire shift with unconditional probability greater than 0.98 under either delivery process specified below. On every execution branch, total samples, exactly 2^21 n, is O(n), with an absolute constant and envelope growth index exactly 0. This guarantee holds jointly with the other resource and tolerance claims.

For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the equatorial sign transcript algorithm in proof.md recovers the entire shift with unconditional probability greater than 0.98 under either delivery process specified below. The tolerated fraction is epsilon(n)=8/25 of all 2^21 n deliveries. The realized corruption count is at most floor((8/25) 2^21 n) on every execution branch. The learner acquires exactly 2^21 n deliveries of the specified register dimensions. Either the supplier fixes the corrupted positions before acquisition and the joint clean marginal is a product of ideal DCP states for the same shift, or at each delivery the supplier chooses whether to corrupt before the learner uses fresh private randomness and measurements for that delivery. In the adaptive case the choice may depend on the full past transcript, and conditional on that choice and past each clean copy is the ideal DCP state for the same shift independent of supplier memory. Corrupt states may be arbitrary and correlated with the supplier. The adaptive supplier has no access to delivered registers. The algorithm does not know the delivery process or the corrupted positions. All four resource bounds hold jointly.
